tex_content.html:
Theorem
1. ch4:4.3,ch4:4.10\group ch04-poisson-newtonian-potential Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0068 Let $\Omega $ be bounded and every boundary point regular for the Laplacian. If $f$ is bounded and locally Hölder in $\Omega $, then \[ \Delta u=f\quad \hbox{in }\Omega , \qquad u=\varphi \quad \hbox{on }\partial \Omega \] has a unique classical solution for each continuous $\varphi $. On a ball $B$, this solution is \begin{equation} \tag {4.10} u(x)=\int _{\partial B}K(x,y)\varphi (y)\, ds_y +\int _BG(x,y)f(y)\, dy. \end{equation}
Proof

\sketch If $w$ is the Newtonian potential of $f$, solve the harmonic Dirichlet problem with boundary value $\varphi -w$. Then $u=v+w$; uniqueness is the maximum principle.

□
